findings.finding: The fixes loosen several checks (B30's 409-sentence exemption, B31's "anywhere in backend/services/", case-insensitive matching everywhere) without documenting negative probes — i.e., no evidence that a wrong implementation would still fail these checks. Case-insensitive matching in B37/tour is justified (innerText/text-transform), but B30's "ignore this exact sentence" and B31's broadened scope could let real violations slip through.
findings.suggestion: For each loosened check, add a unit test with an intentionally non-compliant fixture that must stay red (e.g., a 409 message that is not the brief's mandated sentence, a service host outside the allowed package, a hidden-`<option>` click path). The plan mentions unit tests but doesn't specify they cover the negative direction.

findings.finding: visibleText` / banner text counting "visible elements only" needs a concrete definition — hidden via `display:none`? `visibility:hidden`? inside collapsed `<details>`? Playwright's `innerText` already drops non-rendered text, so if `visibleText` is `innerText`-based it may behave differently across browsers/hidden mechanisms. B36-B46 will be flaky or silently wrong if the visibility rule isn't pinned down.
findings.suggestion: Define visibility as "what `innerText` yields" (or use `:visible` selectors) and state it in the helper's docs; add a unit/DOM test with the hidden `<option>` case explicitly.

findings.finding: B39 "keeps the Copy button element" while its label changes to "Copied" — if the check later re-queries by text/accessible name ("Copy"), a re-query after the label flips will fail. Keeping the element handle is the right call, but any locator strategy inside the check must be key/selector-based, not text-based.
findings.suggestion: Verify the retained handle is re-used for all assertions on that button; assert the label transition only once.

findings.finding: SHIPWRIGHT_E2E_RECHECK_PROJECT` pointing at a stale or mismatched build (built from a different commit than the answer key expects) will produce confusing reds that look like harness bugs again — the exact failure mode this change is fixing.
findings.suggestion: Have `recheck` record/validate the built project's version or at least print a clear "built project may be stale" hint when a red could indicate version mismatch; or document in README which build recheck is known-good against.

findings.finding: listRow` clicking by `[data-k]` key: no stated fallback/diagnostic when the key is absent (thread not in visible list — e.g., pagination, virtualization, or filter state). A silent timeout produces a hard-to-diagnose red.
findings.suggestion: Fail fast with a message listing the visible `[data-k]` keys when the target key isn't found.

findings.finding: None specific — test harness only, no product code, no new dependencies. Confirm `recheck` script doesn't gain unintended shell interpolation of the env var into a path/command (use it as an argv/env value, not string-built shell).
findings.suggestion: Pass the path as an argument, not interpolated into a shell string.

findings.finding: B30’s “ignores the brief’s mandated 409 sentence” needs a narrower definition. Excluding a whole matching line or record could hide a real `lessons.md` access that also contains that sentence, violating the requirement that real accesses still fail.
findings.suggestion: Exempt only the mandated response text from the prose scan, while checking actual file-access evidence independently. Add regression cases for the sentence alone, a real access alone, and both together.

findings.finding: The new recheck entry point does not specify behavior when the project variable is missing, points to an invalid directory, or a required check cannot execute. An empty or partially skipped run could look successful.
findings.suggestion: Validate the project path before starting, fail clearly when required artifacts are absent, and return a nonzero exit status for failed checks or an incomplete tour.

findings.finding: A dedicated Playwright project does not by itself guarantee “no pipeline and no model”; shared configuration, global setup, or project dependencies may still invoke them.
findings.suggestion: Verify that the recheck configuration has no pipeline/model setup dependencies. Include a smoke check with model credentials unavailable to confirm the command runs independently.  The targeted locator and text-comparison fixes are sound and appropriately scoped. Tighten B30’s exemption and its regression coverage before proceeding; the recheck observations are small reliability refinements.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: Hidden-element bug class still open in the draft-card recipe (getByText without a visibility filter).
findings.suggestion: Use visibleText for the click and the marker.

findings.finding: listRow depends on data-k, a name taken from the mockups; header comment claims never by names the agent chose.
findings.suggestion: Name data-k as a mockup contract in the header comment.

findings.suggestion: Reword the comment and add /i to posted.

findings.finding: B39 keeps an ElementHandle that a re-rendering framework would detach.
findings.suggestion: Look the button up again by role Copy reply or Copied.

findings.finding: B37 matches the word question anywhere in main, weaker than before.
findings.suggestion: Accepted: the other two labels carry the check.

doubt.disposition: test-harness TypeScript only: no migration, concurrency, cross-plugin import or irreversible operation

findings.finding: AC 1 says "comment-count text counts visible elements only", but only the second half of the disjunction was fixed. `leafCount(b.page, re) >= 2` still counts hidden elements, so if the phone picker's hidden `<option>`s repeat "N comments" text (exactly the bug class this iterate fixes), the check passes via `leafCount` even though neither visible place shows the count — a false pass the harness was supposed to eliminate.
findings.suggestion: Apply the visible filter to the `leafCount` side too (e.g. pass a visible-only variant of the leaf counter, or drop the `leafCount` half and count with `visibleText` alone), or make the assertion require both the row and the header to be visible matches.

findings.finding: The mandated-text carve-out is applied to every file's code text, so any file that happens to contain the sentence "this lesson is already in lessons.md" gets that occurrence removed before the FILE_NAME scan. If a real file access elsewhere is documented in a comment that quotes the full sentence, the `lessons.md` mention inside it is also masked. The unit test only probes the sentence alone, not a masked access sharing a line with it.
findings.suggestion: Narrow the carve-out (e.g. only strip occurrences that are not part of a `FILE_NAME` match context), or accept and document the residual risk; at minimum add a unit case with the sentence and a real access in the same file.

findings.finding: copy.elementHandle()` is grabbed before the click; if the app re-renders the button on click (React-style replace rather than mutate), the stale handle's `innerText` resolves on a detached node and returns `""` via the catch, making the "Copied" check fail against a correct app. The old role lookup would at least have re-queried. This is the same fragility the iterate set out to remove, just inverted.
findings.suggestion: After the click, re-query the button by a stable attribute (e.g. within the thread view's action bar) rather than freezing an `elementHandle`, or verify via a locator scoped to the container that keeps identity across re-renders.

findings.finding: The "no key" fallback branch of `listRow` is only exercised on a page with exactly one row, so it doesn't prove the fallback avoids the hidden `<option>` when multiple `[data-k]` rows exist or the fallback itself mis-selects. A broken fallback (e.g. text lookup without the row constraint) would still pass this test as written, since the test page has no hidden-option ambiguity in the fallback path.
findings.suggestion: Add a hidden `<option>` with a different thread's title and two rows, then assert the fallback clicks the row whose title matches, not any element containing the text.

findings.finding: The CSS attribute selector escapes only `"` and `\` in the key. Thread keys are platform slugs, so this is fine in practice, but if `str(item.key)` were empty the code silently falls back to the text path even when `item.key` was expected — combined with `filter({ hasText: rowTitle })` truncating at 60 chars, two threads whose titles share the first 60 characters would make the fallback open the wrong thread (a real hazard for long HN titles that repeat).
findings.suggestion: In the fallback, additionally assert the clicked row's `data-k` equals the expected key after click (or match on the full title), to guard against the 60-char truncation ambiguity.  Positive notes: B17's `plain` join, B31's package-wide host scan with the per-file outside check preserved, the recheck project wiring (non-zero exit on hard reds, `expect(b.some(...))` guard against an empty run), and the tour fixes (case-insensitive marker, platform re-pick for the Expired filter) all match the acceptance criteria and are covered by real-behavior unit tests, not smoke tests.  Overall: the harness fixes are correct in direction and mostly well-tested, but AC 1 is only half-applied to the comment-count check (hidden elements can still produce a false pass), so ship-with-fixes.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: list-thread` now matches without case, but still never selects a platform or opens a thread. AC5 explicitly requires selecting the right platform. If the selected platform has no Open threads, the recipe reports an unreached state even when another platform has suitable threads.
findings.suggestion: Find an eligible Open thread in the fixture items and explicitly select its platform and visible list row before checking the summary marker.

findings.finding: The `expired` recipe selects the platform, but its title comparison still uses case-sensitive `.includes()`. This leaves AC5 partially implemented: a title displayed through uppercase or lowercase `text-transform` can incorrectly produce “STATE NOT REACHED.”
findings.suggestion: Normalize both the rendered text and expected title to the same case before comparing.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The diff addresses the reported harness failures, but the tour recipes still miss two explicit requirements.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
